guard: the connection-scoped derived membership-feed KV is reopened after endpoint reconnect
why: The mutation deletes the membership-feed cache clear from the rebuild. The suite opens that cache
on the old connection before reconnect, then watches it afterward. Without the clear, the watch
reuses an object bound to the drained connection and fails on the named post-reconnect assertion.

mutations.name: the reconnect keeps the membership-feed KV bound to the closed connection epoch
mutations.expectRed: the membership feed read re-opens on the fresh connection
mutations.cell: the membership feed read re-opens on the fresh connection
mutations.note: The pre-reconnect read populates the cache. Without this clear, the caught post-reconnect read throws closed connection and the suite still reaches its terminal summary.

mutations.name: reconnect drops the membership watch rearm call
mutations.expectRed: the membership feed watch stays live across reconnect
mutations.cell: the membership feed watch stays live across reconnect
mutations.note: The old iterator is retired and the intent never gets a successor, so the post-reconnect membership-rw write produces no callback.

mutations.name: reconnect stops the local membership iterator but leaves its broker consumer
mutations.expectRed: reconnect deletes the predecessor membership consumer instead of accumulating one
mutations.cell: reconnect deletes the predecessor membership consumer instead of accumulating one
mutations.note: Local iterator stop is not broker deletion. The predecessor remains until the ordered consumer inactive threshold while a successor is created.

mutations.name: reconnect drains the old connection before membership consumer deletion finishes
mutations.expectRed: reconnect deletes the predecessor membership consumer instead of accumulating one
mutations.cell: reconnect deletes the predecessor membership consumer instead of accumulating one
mutations.note: clearConnectionScoped schedules consumer deletion. The rebuild must await it while the old connection is still usable; otherwise the delete is lost and the predecessor lingers.
